title: Mental health outcomes associated with the use of amphetamines: A systematic review and meta-analysis

claims.statement: In observational studies, people who use amphetamines, including methamphetamine, have higher odds of psychosis than people who do not: odds ratio 2.0 (95% CI 1.3–3.3; 7 studies, unadjusted) for any use, and for amphetamine use disorder 3.0 (1.9–4.8; 13 studies, unadjusted) or 2.4 (1.6–3.5; 4 studies) after adjustment for demographics, other substance use and premorbid risk. The association was stronger for psychotic symptoms than for diagnosed psychotic disorders, and the level of use that carries risk could not be estimated.
claims.magnitude: Any use OR 2.0 (1.3–3.3), 7 studies, n=3436, I² 80%. Use disorder OR 3.0 (1.9–4.8), 13 studies, I² 90%; adjusted 2.4 (1.6–3.5), 4 studies, I² 35%. Symptoms vs diagnosed disorder (use disorder): OR 4.3 (2.9–6.5) vs 2.3 (1.2–4.7). No absolute risks reported.

claims.statement: Methamphetamine use is associated with depression in observational studies: pooled adjusted odds ratio 1.3 (95% CI 1.2–1.4; 6 studies) for any amphetamine use, and adjusted odds ratios of 1.60 and 1.50 in the two cohorts that followed people over time while adjusting for earlier depressive symptoms. The association was present in general-population samples (OR 2.0) but not within samples of people who use other substances (OR 1.1).
claims.magnitude: Any amphetamine use, adjusted OR 1.3 (1.2–1.4), 6 studies, I² 0% (McKetin et al., 2019). Longitudinal cohorts: OR 1.60 (1.10–2.30) and 1.50 (1.10–2.30) (Leung et al., 2023). Cross-sectional adjusted 1.66 (1.34–2.05; fixed effect, I² 59%).

claims.statement: Amphetamine use disorder is associated with suicidal ideation and attempts: pooled adjusted odds ratio 1.5 (95% CI 1.3–1.8; 4 studies, I² 0%); for any use the adjusted estimate was 1.7 (1.0–2.9). Only one included study examined deaths by suicide.
claims.magnitude: Use disorder adjusted OR 1.5 (1.3–1.8), 4 studies, n=21,753, I² 0%; any use adjusted 1.7 (1.0–2.9), I² 77%; suicide attempts (unadjusted) OR 3.6 (2.2–5.9).

claims.statement: Whether amphetamine use is associated with violence after accounting for other factors is not established: the pooled adjusted odds ratio was 1.4 (95% CI 0.8–2.4; 6 studies), against 2.2 (1.2–4.1) unadjusted; self-reported violent behaviour was associated (OR 3.7) but violent offending was not (OR 1.0), and the violence studies had the lowest quality ratings.
claims.magnitude: Adjusted OR 1.4 (0.8–2.4), 6 studies, I² 25%; unadjusted 2.2 (1.2–4.1), 10 studies, I² 95%; violent behaviour 3.7 (3.1–4.5); violent offending 1.0 (0.4–2.7).
